chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and Ali ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'The woman who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband.'
He said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced. So she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband.'
And he said: 'The reversion is with copulation, or else, it is only one (divorce).'

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: Revocation (of divorce), the act of taking back a wife during the waiting period.
key_terms.بِالْجِمَاعِ: Through sexual intercourse, indicating the condition for valid revocation.
key_terms.تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ: Marrying another husband, the prerequisite for final permissibility.
key_terms.ثُمَّ تُطَلَّقُ: Then she is divorced, indicating the sequence of events required.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for a woman to become permissible to her first husband after two divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific mechanism of 'Tanzil al-Zawjayn' by defining the required sequence as two distinct divorces separated by two valid revocations (raj'ah), a condition derived from the principle of 'Tahil' (making permissible). The Imam emphasizes that revocation is substantiated by sexual intercourse, ensuring the marriage bond is genuinely re-established before the final divorce, thereby preventing the 'small talaq' trick from invalidating the major condition. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of temporary or permanent remarriage after triple talaq.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, and Ali Bin Khalid, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The woman who is not Permissible for her husband until she marries another husband’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is (one) who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced. So she is (one) who is nor Permissible for him until she marries another husband’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The reversion is with the copulation, or else, rather it is one (divorce)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu and Humayd ibn Ziyad from ibn Sama‘ah from Ja‘far ibn Sama‘ah and Ali ibn Khalid from ‘Abd al-Karim from abu Basir who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who cannot become lawful in marriage for her previous husband without marriage with another man.

He (the Imam) said, ‘She is a woman who is divorced, then her husband goes back to her, then is divorced then he goes back to her, then is divorced. She becomes unlawful for him in marriage unless she marries another man.’
He (the Imam) said that going back to her must be for going to bed with her, otherwise, it is only one divorce.’”
